authority: CEO Round 92 directive: 'The AI must choose what simulation to run next based on epistemic value, not just optimization value. The loop should eventually produce: Hypothesis → Physics model → Candidate simulations → Uncertainty/model disagreement → AI chooses most informative simulation → Run → Update surrogate/posterior → Adversarial falsification → Repeat → Physical test → Calibrate → Novelty/invention gate'

core_principle.ceo_directive: The AI loop must be built so that a successful-looking simulation is easier to disprove than to promote.
core_principle.operationalization: The acquisition function must include an ADVERSARIAL component: the AI actively seeks simulations that could DISPROVE its current hypothesis, not just simulations that confirm it.
core_principle.contrast_with_standard_optimization: Standard Bayesian optimization maximizes information gain about the OPTIMUM. The adversarial loop maximizes information gain about the FAILURE BOUNDARY — where does the hypothesis break?

step_1_hypothesis_generation.description: AI generates a hypothesis about the physical system (e.g., 'this material will not fracture below 15% strain under these BCs')
step_1_hypothesis_generation.input: Current surrogate model, existing simulation results, physics constraints
step_1_hypothesis_generation.output: Formal hypothesis H with quantified confidence
step_1_hypothesis_generation.method: LLM-based reasoning (OX Alpha) over simulation history + physics knowledge

step_2_physics_model_selection.description: Select the appropriate physics model from the validated ladder (L3-L8)
step_2_physics_model_selection.constraint: Must use the HIGHEST validated physics level (cannot use L7 FSI if only L3 is validated)

step_3_candidate_simulation_generation.description: Generate a set of candidate simulations (parameter combinations) that could test the hypothesis
step_3_candidate_simulation_generation.method: Latin hypercube sampling + adversarial sampling (samples near expected failure boundary)
step_3_candidate_simulation_generation.output: N candidate simulations with predicted outcomes and uncertainty

step_4_uncertainty_quantification.description: For each candidate, quantify the uncertainty in the prediction
types: Epistemic uncertainty (model form) — from surrogate model variance
Aleatory uncertainty (parameter) — from input parameter distributions
Discretization uncertainty — from mesh/time step refinement
step_4_uncertainty_quantification.method: Gaussian Process posterior variance + polynomial chaos expansion

step_5_ai_chooses_most_informative_simul.description: The AI selects the simulation that maximally tests the hypothesis
step_5_ai_chooses_most_informative_simul.acquisition_function: Expected Information Gain (EIG) weighted by adversarial value
step_5_ai_chooses_most_informative_simul.formula: EIG(x) = H[p(y|x)] - E_{y}[H[p(y|x,y)]] where H is entropy. Adversarial weighting: EIG_adv(x) = EIG(x) * P(failure|x) where P(failure|x) is the predicted probability that the hypothesis FAILS at x.
step_5_ai_chooses_most_informative_simul.key_innovation: The adversarial weighting means the AI prefers simulations where the hypothesis is MOST LIKELY TO FAIL, not where it is most likely to succeed. This implements the CEO directive: 'easier to disprove than to promote.'

step_6_run_simulation.description: Execute the selected simulation using the validated physics substrate
step_6_run_simulation.constraint: Must use FEBio + SfePy cross-solver validation (L3+ discipline)

step_7_update_surrogate_posterior.description: Update the surrogate model with the new data point
step_7_update_surrogate_posterior.method: Bayesian update of Gaussian Process (or deep kernel learning for high-D)
step_7_update_surrogate_posterior.output: Updated surrogate model with reduced uncertainty near x*

step_8_adversarial_falsification.description: Check if the new result FALSIFIES the hypothesis
step_8_adversarial_falsification.test: If y* falls outside the predicted confidence interval, OR if the hypothesis predicted success but failure occurred, the hypothesis is FALSIFIED
step_8_adversarial_falsification.action_on_falsification: Record the falsification in the cemetery (CE-XXX), generate a new hypothesis that accounts for the failure mode
step_8_adversarial_falsification.action_on_confirmation: Increase confidence in hypothesis, but ALSO increase the adversarial weight for future simulations (try harder to break it)

step_9_repeat_or_escalate.description: If hypothesis survives N rounds of adversarial testing, escalate to physical experiment
step_9_repeat_or_escalate.threshold: Hypothesis must survive 10 adversarial simulations with no falsification before physical testing is authorized

step_10_physical_test.description: Design and execute a physical experiment to calibrate/validate the simulation
step_10_physical_test.constraint: Must follow Article XXXIV (stop coding when reality is the next bottleneck)

step_11_calibrate.description: Use experimental data to calibrate the simulation model
step_11_calibrate.method: Bayesian calibration (Kennedy-O'Hagan framework) — accounts for model discrepancy
step_11_calibrate.output: Calibrated model with updated parameter posterior

step_12_novelty_invention_gate.description: If the calibrated model reveals a novel mechanism or design that survives adversarial testing AND physical validation, declare a candidate invention
step_12_novelty_invention_gate.gate: Article XXXV completion loop — the candidate must be able to generate its own next falsification experiment

connection_to_physics_ladder.L3_hyperelasticity: VALIDATED — provides the base elastic model for the surrogate
connection_to_physics_ladder.L5_damage: PLANNED — adds material degradation (needed for fracture prediction)
connection_to_physics_ladder.L6_contact: PLANNED — adds multi-body interaction (needed for clot-device contact)
connection_to_physics_ladder.L7_FSI: PLANNED — adds fluid-structure interaction (needed for blood flow + clot)
connection_to_physics_ladder.L8_fracture: PLANNED — adds fracture/fragmentation (the Slot 5 invention target)
connection_to_physics_ladder.principle: The AI loop can only use physics capabilities that have been VALIDATED via the CEAT-GATE. It cannot use L7 FSI to test a hypothesis if L7 has not passed CEAT.

implementation_plan.phase_4_round_100+: Add physical experiment interface (Article XXXIV trigger). First calibrated simulation.

python_implementation.adversarial_sampling: Custom implementation — samples near predicted failure boundary
python_implementation.orchestration: Custom Python orchestrator that calls FEBio/SfePy and manages the loop

key_difference_from_standard_Bayesian_op.standard_BO: Maximizes information about the OPTIMUM (where is the best parameter setting?)
key_difference_from_standard_Bayesian_op.adversarial_loop: Maximizes information about the FAILURE BOUNDARY (where does the hypothesis break?)
key_difference_from_standard_Bayesian_op.implication: The AI will preferentially sample regions where the model is MOST uncertain about whether the hypothesis holds, not where the model predicts the best outcome. This is the operationalization of 'easier to disprove than to promote.'
